findings.reason: without a declared order or `plan-section-depends-on`, §11 and §13 are dispatchable in the same beat against one file, and the collision surfaces only as a merge conflict after both gates have passed.
findings.text: §13 declares `reckon/crew/gc.py` as an exclusive write path, and the still-open §11 (line 171) declares the same file plus an operational `crew gc --apply` pass that reads the same region of `garbage_collect`; both sections are `data-status="implementable"` and both have open followups (`f-tchhab-011`, `f-tchhab-013`), so a coordinator dispatching the two together gets two workers writing `gc.py` in separate worktrees with no declared order — while the plan serialises every other same-module pair in prose (`after §2`, `after §3`, `after §6`)

findings.reason: the root cause §13 acts on ("nothing removes the memo entries") is unaffected, and the deliverable no longer borrows any pick-input rule, so a builder reads the clause as motivation and the explicit mechanism beside it as the instruction.
findings.text: the Why says `reckon/crew/gc.py` "sweeps the pick-input and ledger caches", but the only cache sweep in the file matches `ledger-*.sqlite` under `cache_root("pick-input")` and its own docstring records that the picker's `picker-*.json` inputs "in the same root are untouched" (`reckon/crew/gc.py:407,421`), so the clause repeats a loose phrase from the review it cites rather than describing the code

findings.reason: a memo entry is recomputed on its next miss (`persisted_memo` passes `compute=` at `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:928`), so pruning one from a run-confined pass costs one reparse rather than correctness, and the builder has the guarded neighbour in view.
findings.text: §13 says `crew gc` sweeps the memo store but never states whether the run-confined pass (`crew gc --run <id>`) does, while the hook it must sit beside is guarded on exactly that (`_orphan_ledger_indexes(apply=apply, now=now) if run_id is None else []`, `reckon/crew/gc.py:844`)
